deliverables_scope.text: ===== FILE: files/Attachment_1_-_SOW.pdf ===== REF NO FA252126QB121 1. Purpose and Scope The purpose of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to define the requirements for the procurement, delivery, and potential training associated with a portable, inflatable planetarium system. This system will be utilized to project 360-degree video content and astronomy curriculum to support community and educational outreach. 2. Minimum Technical Requirements The vendor shall provide a complete, portable planetarium system meeting or exceeding the following baseline speciﬁcations: Requirement Category Specification Details Dome Infrastructure Inflatable dome constructed in accordance with published industry standard ASTM F2374-24 (Standard Practice for Design, manufa

t meet commercially recognized safety standards for flame resistance, chemical resistance, and durability. Projection Hardware 4K resolution projector equipped with a fisheye lens (or comparable dome-specific lens). Media Capability System must support projection of standard 360-degree film and video content. REF NO FA252126QB121 Audio System Integrated or portable speaker system capable of delivering clear sound inside the dome, synced with the media projection system required. Power Compatibility All hardware (projector, blower, audio, laptop) must operate on standard US 110V/120V AC power. 3. Safety, Capacity, & Support Requirements To ensure personnel safety and long-term system viability, the procurement must satisfy the following parameters: Category Requirement Details Capacity The 5-meter dome must comfortably accommodate a minimum seating capacity of 25 adults. Safety Features The dome must feature clearly marked emergency exit points. Ventilation Adequate air exchange and ventilation must be maintained to ensure occupant comfort during operation. Warranty Minimum of a 1-year comprehensive warranty covering parts and labor for the dome fabric, blower, and projector. Technical Support Access to vendor-provided technical support during standard busine

re or services (including those manufactured by Huawei, ZTE, Hikvision, Dahua, or Hytera) are included in any part of the delivered system (projector, computer, software, cameras). All electronic and specialized hardware delivered under this contract must be Trade Agreements Act (TAA) compliant, meaning they are manufactured or substantially transformed in the United States or a designated country. Complete product packages must be delivered within 120 Days after date of award. Delivery will be FOB Destination to Patrick SFB, Florida. Full delivery information and address to be provided upon award. Delivery cost to be included with deliverable items in vendor quote. ===== FILE: files/Planetarium_QA-1.docx ===== Section 2 Requires the inflatable dome to be constructed in accordance with ASTM F2374-24. Can the Government clarify whether compliance must be demonstrated through formal third-party testing/certification, or if a manufacture’s written certification or statement that the offered dome was designed and manufactured in accordance with ASTM F2374-24 will satisfy the requirement? “Compliance with ASTM F2374-24 or equivalent recognized standard for temporary membrane/inflatable structures is acceptable.” The respective party to offer should back the respective certification

ective certification. Whether they provide the certification directly or state a manufactuer certification does not matter so long as the certification is present and shown in the offer and backed by the offeror. The SOW states that “all electronic and specialized hardware” must be TAA compliant, while the solicitation states that the items must be TAA and Buy American compliant. Would an inflatable planetarium system be acceptable if the inflatable dome itself is manufactured in China, but the complete planetarium system is assembled in the United States and all electronic/specialized hardware complies with the applicable TAA/Buy American requirements? TAA Compliance and Buy American both apply. Buy American and TAA Compliance are a matter of final product as well as components. To that end the projector and computer are standalone systems and needs to be fully compliant with Buy American and TAA Compliance regulation. The inflatable dome however is incomplete as a planetarium without those systems and so can be considered just a component of the end product. To that end the majority of the cost should be in the projector, computer, and related software with training. A 4-server GPU/CPU rack capable of multi-threaded processing, GPU-accelerated workloads, AI and simulation applications, and integration with a system equivalent to Omniverse-based digital twin and simulation environments 2. A control workstation for remote monitoring, asset management, and system integration with the server rack. All systems and services must be fully compatible, ope rational, and support in tegrated management workflows. All deliverables, includi ng server systems, GPUs and CPUs, storage, memory, networking, and supporting infrastructure, shall be fully assembled, configured, tested, and operational. Please identify the required level, or confirm that no CMMC requirement applies to this acquisition. Answer 11: There is no CMMC for this requirement. Question 12: CLIN 0002 configuration. Please confirm that CLIN 0002 is to be quoted as a complete, assembled system rather than as component parts. Answer 12: This should be quoted as a complete assembled system. Question 13: Warranty, support, and subscription duration. Sections covering warranty, on-site support, and NVIDIA Omniverse Enterprise subscriptions each state a duration of "one- to three-year." Because award is on a lowest-price technically acceptable basis, this range materially affects evaluated price. Will the Government specify a single required duration for each of these items, or state that quoters should price a defined baseline period? Introduction and Overview Patoka River National Wildlife Refuge and Management Area (Refuge) was established in 1994 in Pike and Gibson Counties to conserve and manage habitat for waterfowl and other migratory birds, resident wildlife, and endangered and threatened species. Active habitat management of wetland, forest, and prairie habitats occur on the nearly 13,000 acres acquired to date. The refuge offers public hunting and fishing, wildlife viewing and photography, environmental education and interpretation. The refuge headquarters is located in Oakland City, IN. The BEL and Bruce tracts are adjacent properties located in Pike County off CR 850E north of Francisco, IN and south of the Patoka River. The nearest crossroads are CR 850E and CR 50 N The Hughes tract is in Gibson county north of Francisco, IN and south of the Patoka River on CR 750E.
